analysis.title: weekly mash (Mark Wilson, 30 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Wilson had argued that hyperscaler results this week and the US midterms next week were peak event risk, and that clearing both would allow a year-end rally led by the biggest index stocks. He calls the past two weeks a bruising test of that view.

Hyperscaler cloud growth is accelerating. Alphabet cloud revenue grew 103% y/y and its backlog 256% y/y ($120b annual run-rate revenue, $561b backlog). AWS grew 39% with backlog up 189% y/y to $578b. Azure grew 48%, held back by supply, and Microsoft expects acceleration next quarter as supply improves.

Amazon management expects AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028 and says it has visibility into 2027, 2028 and part of 2029. Jassy said 85% of global IT spend is still on premises, which Wilson takes as a large runway.

Financing visibility improved. META completed the first two legs (common stock and convertible) of a three-part record equity raise. Oracle pulled forward its cash flow breakeven forecast and said it needs only $20b of financing to deliver its capex plans.

2026 capex plans stayed stable for the first quarter in some time and 2027 expectations were little changed. Wilson judges the financing gap well below what was feared a week ago, and US 10-year yields have fallen four weeks running.

Cyber risk is rising as AI tools and a larger attack surface expand opportunities for hackers. Binance suffered what Wilson calls the largest heist in history late in the week. Jassy suggested security could take a significant share, perhaps 20%, of tokens used over the next year or two.

Nasdaq was down more than 3.5% on the day as Wilson wrote, on bad news from Intel, concern about certain software names, and questions over Alphabet's search and Amazon's retail businesses. He argues the market may weigh the three positives above differently in coming days and weeks, and says news on capex, operating cash flow and funding gaps has been positive in earnings so far.

The AI-winners versus AI-at-risk basket pair, which traded a low-volatility trend through the first half, is now down on the year. The Mag7/hyperscaler outperformance that began in late June was also dented this week.

Stock correlations have broken down. Apple is negatively correlated to the Nasdaq and S&P equal-weight has only a 60% correlation to the S&P 500. The S&P ex-AI beat the Nasdaq by more than 3% on the week and France's CAC beat US tech by 5%. The S&P 500 fell 30bps on a day when 80% of constituents rose.

Wilson sees no sign of a demand slowdown. Token demand, chip pricing, rental yields and useful-life assumptions are all rising, and supply-side worries are about capacity constraints rather than overshoot. He would watch for a slowdown in demand or excess capacity as the signal of a cyclical shift.

He calls the 2007/2008 credit analogy for the neocloud and financing story misplaced, but says the 1990s question of whether this is 1997 or 1999 is relevant. Goldman work on macro assets in Fed hiking cycles suggests three months of equity indigestion does not change the trend.

Capex growth quarter on quarter may have paused for now with a focus on efficiency. Wilson says that requires more discretion on 2027 winners but that reports of the AI capex demise and funding threat look greatly exaggerated. He sees continued de-risking before the midterms as understandable and as raising the opportunity once known risks clear.

market_movers.rationale: Cloud revenue +103% y/y and backlog +256% y/y are cited as evidence of accelerating cloud growth. Wilson also notes lingering questions on the core search business.
Azure grew 48% while supply-constrained and management expects acceleration as supply improves. Copilot usage metrics cited as rising quickly.
AWS backlog +189% y/y to $578b and management guides to AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. Wilson also flags concern about the retail business.
Completed the first two legs of a three-part record equity raise, which Wilson counts as improved financing visibility.
Brought forward its cash flow breakeven forecast and said it needs only $20b of financing for its capex plans.
Named as a source of objectively bad news that contributed to the Nasdaq's decline on the day. No detail on the news is given.

sector_views.rationale: Wilson says hyperscaler ROI is revealing itself clearly and capex and funding fears look exaggerated, though he expects greater discretion is needed among 2027 winners. This is a thematic read rather than a formal sector rating.

earnings_insights: Alphabet, reported this week: cloud revenue +103% y/y, annual run-rate about $120b, revenue backlog +256% y/y to $561b.
Microsoft, reported this week: Azure growth 48%, constrained by supply. Management expects growth to accelerate next quarter as supply improves.

Amazon, reported this week: AWS growth 39% in the quarter, backlog +189% y/y to $578b. Management expressed confidence in AWS revenue growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. Revenue commitments for Graviton and Trainium each rose more than 20x y/y.
Meta: completed the first two legs (common and convertible) of a three-part record equity raise.
Oracle financial update: brought forward its forecast date for cash flow breakeven and said only $20b of financing is required for its intended capex plans.

Across hyperscalers, 2026 capex plans stayed stable this quarter and 2027 expectations are little changed. Wilson keeps a sheet tracking capex plans, operating cash flow and remaining funding gaps and says news on all three has been positive so far this earnings season.
Intel results were described as objectively bad news. No figures are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Falling yields ease the cost-of-capital concern that Wilson says has weighed on equities and AI financing.
Listed among the non-AI developments in the world, alongside a crude oil rally and Middle East energy logistics complications.

crypto_views: Binance fell victim to what the note calls the largest heist in history late in the week, cited as part of a rising cyber risk environment.
risk_factors: A slowdown in AI demand or signs of excess capacity, which Wilson says are not detectable today.
Financing risk and the neocloud credit story, including the cost of capital weighing on equities.
Discretion needed on 2027 winners, since capex growth may have paused.
Event risk from the US midterms next week and from Brazil, Israel and UK budget developments.
Energy risk from Middle East logistics, a crude rally and higher European gas prices.
Rising cyber risk from AI tooling and a larger attack surface.
Core business questions for Alphabet search and Amazon retail, concern about certain software names, and Intel's bad news.
charts_described: First chart: the AI-winners versus AI-at-risk basket pair, which traded a low-volatility trend through the first half, is now down on the year and struggling for direction.
Second chart: Mag7 and hyperscaler outperformance versus the index since late June, which was dented this week.
Later chart (from Brian Garrett, US derivatives): shows how unusual it is for the S&P 500 to fall 30bps when 80% of constituents are up on the day.
Chart from Vickie Chang's work on macro assets in Fed hiking cycles: Wilson reads the lesson as three months of equity indigestion not changing the trend.
vol_and_positioning: The AI-winners versus AI-at-risk basket pair traded a low-volatility trend through the first half of the year. It is now down on the year and struggling for direction.
Mag7 and hyperscalers had outperformed the index since the prior trend broke in late June. That trend was dented this week.
Stock correlations have broken down. Apple is negatively correlated to the Nasdaq and S&P equal-weight has only a 60% correlation to the S&P 500.
The S&P ex-AI outperformed the Nasdaq by more than 3% on the week. The S&P 500 fell 30bps on a day when 80% of its constituents rose, which Wilson calls very unusual.
Trading has been hard for weeks and investors are continuing to de-risk ahead of the midterms. Wilson says that raises the potential opportunity once known unknowns clear.
geopolitical: Complications of Middle East energy logistics, with a crude rally and a quick three-month doubling of European gas prices

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler cloud growth is accelerating with backlogs up 189% to 256% y/y, token demand, chip pricing and rental yields are rising, and management cites faster capex payback and visibility into 2027 and 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: The market sold off despite results, with Nasdaq down more than 3.5% on the day. Concerns include Intel's bad news, software names, Alphabet search and Amazon retail, the cost of capital, and doubts about capital misallocation (the 1997 versus 1999 question).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Signs of slowing demand or supply-side overshoot as excess capacity becomes evident, which Wilson says is not visible today.

tension_points.bull_case: Meta's equity raise and Oracle's $20b financing need show a financing gap smaller than feared, 2026 capex plans are stable and US 10-year yields have fallen four weeks running.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher cost of capital has hampered equities in recent months and neocloud credit worries drew comparisons with 2007/2008.

theme_stances.key_argument: Clearing hyperscaler earnings and the midterms would likely allow a year-end rally, though the past two weeks have been a bruising test of that view.
